title: Formulary Coverage Rule and Formulary Exceptions on Insulin Pharmacy Payer Tiers
content:
An insulin is covered on a payer tier of the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program only when it is on the tier's preferred insulin list or the payer has approved a formulary exception for it, recorded as an authorization grant with basis payer prior authorization for that item; the self-pay tier lists every insulin.

## Formulary rule

1. **Coverage.** On a payer tier, an insulin is covered when either holds: it is on the tier's preferred insulin list, or an approved formulary exception for that item is recorded as an authorization grant with basis payer prior authorization. This is read from the tier's list and the program's authorization records for that item.
2. **Exception requests.** A formulary exception request is sent to the payer when the prescriber states that the preferred insulins are not appropriate for the customer; it is decided within the tier's standard decision time in days (or its expedited decision time in hours when expedited) and is valid for the tier's formulary exception validity in calendar months.
3. **Part D and MA-PD.** On the Part D and MA-PD tiers the exception request is the plan's coverage determination, and a customer becomes liable for a non-covered insulin only after the plan's coverage determination denies it.
4. **Until an exception is approved.** Until an exception is approved the customer may switch to a preferred insulin on a new prescription or buy the requested insulin at the item's Larkfield cash price.

## Coverage on a payer tier

| On the tier's preferred list | Approved exception recorded for the item | Covered |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes |
| No | No | No — the customer may switch to a preferred insulin on a new prescription or buy the requested insulin at the cash price |

## Questions the rule answers

*Does the self-pay tier need exceptions?* No; the self-pay tier lists every insulin.

*When does a Part D or MA-PD customer become liable for a non-covered insulin?* Only after the plan's coverage determination denies it.
